meta.title: Moba - a free AI-first coding school
meta.description: Free programming lectures, live on Twitch and recorded on YouTube. We learn with AI from day one, then build projects together that solve real problems.

hero.eyebrow: Free coding school · live on Twitch
hero.titleLead: Learn to code for a world where AI writes code too.
hero.titleAccent: Free, from the basics to projects people actually use.
hero.lead: Lectures stream live on Twitch, and the recordings stay on YouTube. You learn with a Claude framework I designed for you. It walks you through problems but doesn't solve them for you. Once you have the basics, we build projects together that solve real problems.

demo.caption: The framework doesn't write code for you. It guides you until you understand.

name.label: Why Moba
name.definition: An old Serbian custom of mutual help. When someone needed to harvest wheat, mow a meadow or build a house, the neighbors gathered and worked together, without pay. Work one family couldn't manage alone got done by everyone together.
name.why: We do the same. We learn together, for free, and then together we build what the people around us need.
name.principle: Many courses convince you that programming pays very well, and then charge you to learn it. That makes no sense to me. If knowledge is truly valuable, whoever has it doesn't need to sell it. We teach because we want to share that gift with others, not to earn from the lectures.
name.support: That doesn't mean we'll turn down donations, investment or other support from those who want to help. The point is that we never make knowledge conditional on a mandatory fee.
name.quote: “I give of my talents freely, and I am wonderfully blessed financially.”
name.quoteSource: Joseph Murphy, The Power of Your Subconscious Mind

problem.label: Problem
problem.title: Serbia has plenty of coding courses. Most share the same three flaws.

items.title: They're expensive
items.text: A good course often costs more than most people can spare. Without the money, you're left out, however motivated you are.

items.title: They stop at the basics
items.text: You finish with a certificate and a few exercises. No real project, no team, no experience you can show.

items.title: AI is an afterthought
items.text: AI is now part of a developer's everyday work, yet few courses use it seriously. If they mention it at all, it's in passing. Or they use it to finish the whole project without a proper explanation, which undermines learning.

items.title: Free. All of it.
items.text: Lectures stream live on Twitch, where you ask questions in real time. Every recording then goes to YouTube. Nobody pays a single dinar to access anything.

items.title: AI first
items.text: From day one you work with Claude and a framework I built for learning. It doesn't solve problems for you; it makes you understand them. Every project we build rests on it.

items.title: Real projects, real problems
items.text: After the lectures, we work on real projects together. You see what a project looks like from idea to launch.

plan.label: Plan
plan.title: Knowledge first, then experience
plan.intro: The program has two phases, one after the other. The lectures give you knowledge; the projects give you experience you can't get from lectures. Together they make you a developer.

phases.title: Learning
phases.subtitle: You learn the foundations, live and for free.
phases.text: Lectures stream live on Twitch, from web basics to full-stack applications. Between lectures you practice with the Claude framework, which guides you through every problem until you understand it.
benefits: Knowledge you understand, not code you copied.
The habit of using AI as a tool, not a shortcut.
A recording of every lecture to come back to whenever you need.
People learning the same things, so nobody learns alone.

phases.title: Projects
phases.subtitle: We build something of real value.
phases.text: Once you have the basics, we pick a project together that solves an existing problem, and we build it from scratch. Not an exercise that ends up in a drawer, but something people will actually use.
benefits: A say in which project we build.
Experience solving a problem that actually exists.
A view of a project's whole journey, from scratch to launch.
A project you can show in a job interview.

program.label: Program
program.title: Learning in four stages
program.intro: The first phase is split into four stages. Each builds on the one before and ends with projects you build on your own, with the Claude framework. You start with how the web works and finish with a full-stack application.
program.outro: After the fourth stage, phase 2 begins: we build real projects together.
program.disclaimer: This plan isn't final. Stages, topics and projects may change before the lectures begin.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.subtitle: From zero to your first interactive page.
stages.text: You set up your tools and learn how the web works. You write your first pages in HTML and CSS, then bring them to life with JavaScript.

stages.title: JavaScript
stages.subtitle: From a script to a well-organized app.
stages.text: You learn to write code that grows without chaos: objects, classes and modules, the tools professionals use, working with APIs, and tests. Algorithms and data structures come at the end.
projects: Linked list, hash map and binary search tree

stages.title: React
stages.subtitle: User interfaces the way they are built today.
stages.text: You move to the library behind a large share of today's web apps. You learn to break an app into components, manage state and connect multiple pages.

stages.title: Node.js and databases
stages.subtitle: A server, a database and an app on the internet.
stages.text: You write the server side of an application: how data is stored, how users log in and how the app gets online. The stage ends with a large full-stack project.

ai.label: AI first
ai.title: The Claude framework: AI that teaches you, not works for you
ai.intro: I'm building the framework for Claude, Anthropic's AI assistant. It's still in progress; these are the principles behind it.

items.title: A question instead of a finished answer.
items.text: When you're stuck, you don't get code. You get questions and hints that lead you until you reach the solution yourself.

items.title: You learn from the problem you're solving.
items.text: No made-up exercises. You learn exactly what the task in front of you needs, right when you need it.

items.title: You must be able to explain every line.
items.text: Before moving on, you explain what your code does and why. Code you don't understand isn't yours.

items.title: The same tool in class and on the project.
items.text: The framework underpins every project we build, so the habits you form in lectures carry straight into real work.

projects.label: Projects
projects.title: What do we build? We decide together.
projects.intro: The lectures aren't the end; they're the preparation. Afterwards we build projects chosen from proposed problems in everyday life.

stages.title: You propose
stages.text: Anyone can propose a problem worth solving: in their town, their field or their community.

stages.title: We choose together
stages.text: Proposals are discussed in the open, and participants decide which project we build.

stages.title: We build
stages.text: I build the project and set the tasks, with help from participants. Everyone can follow along as the project comes together, step by step.

stages.title: We ship
stages.text: A commercial product or a public good. What matters is that it brings people real value.
